tagline: The historic heart of three empires — Hagia Sophia, the Blue Mosque, Topkapı Palace, and the Grand Bazaar all within walking distance.

items.name: Çorlulu Ali Paşa Medresesi
items.description: A beautifully preserved Ottoman courtyard off the Grand Bazaar turned into a shaded tea garden. One of the great hidden spots in historic Istanbul.
items.tip: Duck through the small gate on Yeniçeriler Caddesi — most tourists walk straight past it. Order nargileh (water pipe) and çay and settle in.

items.name: Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi Çay Bahçesi
items.description: The tea garden adjacent to the famous köfte restaurant, with views of the old city. Good for resting between sights.

items.name: Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi
items.description: Istanbul's most legendary köfte restaurant, open since 1920. One dish, done perfectly. A genuine institution.
items.tip: Order the köfte with white beans (piyaz) and bread. Sit, eat, leave. This is not a restaurant for lingering — and that's the point.

items.name: Balıkçı Sabahattin
items.description: One of Istanbul's most atmospheric fish restaurants, set in a historic Ottoman house near the city walls. Exceptional mezes.
items.tip: Book ahead and go for lunch — quieter than dinner and the same quality. The mezes are as good as the main course.

items.name: Hagia Sophia
items.description: The greatest building in Istanbul — perhaps in the world. 1,500 years of history in a single structure. Free to enter as a mosque.
items.tip: Go at opening time (9am) or in the last hour before closing. The midday crowds are genuinely overwhelming. Dress modestly.

items.name: Topkapı Palace
items.description: The nerve centre of the Ottoman Empire for 400 years. The Treasury and the Harem are the unmissable sections.
items.tip: Buy the combined museum pass — it covers Topkapı, Hagia Sophia, and the Archaeology Museum. Book Harem entry separately online.

items.name: Basilica Cistern
items.description: A vast underground Byzantine cistern built in 532 AD — columns rising from still water in eerie, lit silence. Genuinely spectacular.

items.name: Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii)
items.description: The iconic six-minaret mosque facing Hagia Sophia across the hippodrome. Free to enter outside prayer times.
items.tip: Closed to non-worshippers during prayer times (5 times daily). The interior is beautiful but often crowded — Hagia Sophia is more impressive.

tips: Sultanahmet is walkable from Eminönü and 10 minutes by tram (T1 line) from Karaköy.
The area is almost entirely tourist-facing — prices for food and services are significantly higher than elsewhere in Istanbul.
The best time to visit the major monuments is early morning (before 10am) or late afternoon (after 4pm).
Combine Sultanahmet with a walk down to Cankurtaran and the sea walls for a much quieter Istanbul experience.
